evidence.claims: Checked: effective rate, break-even and target gap (llms.txt:3, README.md:3-6) are produced and correct; 'break-even' is explicitly labelled 'direct costs only' (quote_margin.py:307), so it is honest though non-standard; 'the CLI and the page share one arithmetic; a test runs both' (llms.txt) backed by parity.test.mjs and test_quote_margin.py:363; no-warranty / not-advice disclaimer present (README, index.html:401, guides); 'does not recommend prices' honoured throughout; vs-bonsai.html explicitly declines to state Bonsai prices it could not verify and carries a not-affiliated note. Gaps: README.md:14 'Not yet deployed' contradicts the live link; the product is named 'Quote Margin Check' and calculate() is documented as 'the transparent margin report' (calc.mjs:49) but no margin % is output anywhere; 'small agencies' (README.md:4, VENTURE.yaml:2) is claimed but staff labor cost is not modelled.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a freelancer with a $2,400 fixed quote wants to know what it pays per hour once admin and revisions count, and what to say to a 10% discount ask. The page/CLI answer both directly ($54.86/h; 10% off -> $48.00/h, or cut 12.6 h of scope to hold $75), with overrun, cost-rise and kill-fee tables a freelancer would actually use mid-negotiation. A small agency with paid staff cannot enter labor cost per person, and a freelancer on a platform with a percentage fee has to approximate it as a fixed amount.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard freelance pricing practice (effective hourly rate including non-billable time) and with small-business estimating practice (gross margin % on price, margin vs markup, cost-plus with fees grossed up). The effective-rate and target-price method is the standard one and correct. Departs: (1) no gross margin % (cost_coverage / price) or markup %, the first number a controller asks for of a tool called 'margin check' (example: 1920/2400 = 80.0% margin after direct costs, 400% markup on them); (2) percentage-of-price costs (platform fees, card processing, sales commissions) cannot be expressed, so target price and discount tables treat them as fixed; (3) subcontractor cost passes through at cost with no markup option, while agencies typically mark up subs; (4) the kill fee is modelled as on top of the deposit, whereas many contracts credit the deposit against it (labelled on the page, so low).

defects.what: A tool named 'Quote Margin Check' reports no margin: calculate() has no gross margin % (cost_coverage / price) or markup %, in the CLI or the page, so a controller cannot read the standard figure or see the margin-vs-markup distinction (example: 80.0% margin, 400% markup on direct costs).

Costs that scale with price (platform service fees, card processing, commissions) can only be typed as a fixed overhead amount, so the target price is understated (10% fee: 3345 vs grossed-up 3450) and the discount table keeps the fee constant as the price falls.
README says the page is 'Not yet deployed to a public URL' four lines after giving the live marisstella.app link.
Exact-zero boundaries untested: survives_overrun_percent's >= 0 and the discount table's cost_coverage > 0 can both flip without any test failing.
'Small agencies' is claimed but there is no staff labor cost input; an agency's own employees can only be modelled as a single owner target rate.

verdict: Every figure recomputed by hand matched the shipped code (effective rate 54.86, target 3,105, buffer 3,630, cost-rise 51.43/3,225, 10% discount 48.00 with a 12.6 h scope cut, kill-fee paths 1,920/1,380/1,020), and the CLI and browser are pinned to each other by an exact parity test; 172 tests pass and 3 of 5 seeded mutants were caught, the two survivors being exact-zero boundaries. The method is the standard freelance effective-rate one and the copy is careful not to overclaim. Where a small-business controller would stop: a 'margin check' that never shows a margin %, no way to express fees that scale with price, and no staff labor cost for the 'small agencies' it names. A README line still says the page is undeployed. Meets the bar for a freelancer's quote worksheet; domain sits at 2 until margin % and percentage fees are modelled.
